source_caption:
The “Shrek in the Swamp Karaoke Dance Party” was originally created as a three-minute musical short for the film’s 2001 VHS and DVD releases, but its massive popularity accidentally pioneered the “animated dance party ending” trope that dominated 2000s family films. While the sequence brought back almost the entire principal voice cast to record their own singing lines, there was one notable exception: Eddie Murphy did not return to record Donkey’s rendition of “Baby Got Back”. Instead, the production brought in Mark Moseley, an impressionist and Murphy’s former voice double, to seamlessly replicate Donkey’s vocals. Additionally, the animators used the chaotic musical finale to playfully retcon the fates of characters presumed dead, notably revealing Lord Farquaad singing “Stayin’ Alive” from inside Dragon’s stomach and Mama Bear—who had previously been depicted as a tragic bearskin rug in Farquaad’s castle—dancing along perfectly alive.

Shrek (2001), directed by Andrew Adamson and Vicky Jenson, starring Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz, John Lithgow. A bitter, reclusive ogre’s peaceful swamp is suddenly overrun by exiled fairy tale creatures, forcing him to strike a deal with a ruthless lord and embark on a quest to rescue a princess who harbors a dark secret of her own.

source_details.synopsis: Shrek is a 2001 American animated fantasy comedy film directed by Andrew Adamson and Vicky Jenson, and written by Ted Elliott, Terry Rossio, Joe Stillman, and Roger S. H. Schulman, loosely based on the 1990 children's picture book Shrek! by William Steig. It is the first installment in the Shrek film series, and stars Mike Myers, Eddie Murphy, Cameron Diaz and John Lithgow. In the film, an embittered ogre named Shrek (voiced by Myers) finds his home in the swamp overrun by fairy tale creatures banished by the obsessive ruler Lord Farquaad (Lithgow).
